title: Counted or present?
hook: A count can miss members of the population.

knows: Animals depend on features of their surroundings.
doesNotKnow: In a toy habitat known to contain 10 animals, a survey detects 5. How many were present but not detected?

misconception: A single observation or change determines the same outcome everywhere.
objective: In a toy habitat known to contain 10 animals, a survey detects 5. How many were present but not detected?

claims.text: In a toy habitat known to contain 10 animals, a survey detects 5. How many were present but not detected? The stipulated population contains 10 animals and the survey detects 5, leaving 10 − 5 = 5 not detected. Real surveys usually do not know the total beforehand, so a raw count alone does not reveal how many were missed.
claims.source: Stipulated illustrative scenario, not wildlife observations. Source lead, not checked: OpenStax Biology 2e, ecology, https://openstax.org/details/books/biology-2e

claims.text: The panels show a simplified illustrative scenario, not observations or measurements of real animals.
A toy population contains 12 animals and 7 are detected. How many are missed? 12 present minus 7 detected leaves 5 missed.
